title: TPS variance prober and regression bisector
creator: Maya Chen
description: Purpose: Build a reproducible, low-noise harness that probes tokens-per-second (TPS) variance across core models and automatically bisects regressions to a minimal cause. This ticket covers: (1) new workload generator that exercises cold-start and long-running contexts, (2) p95-aware measurement plumbing with jitter control and warmup heuristics, (3) an automated bisector that narrows regressions to PRs/configs/infra changes, and (4) integration into the Canary/Alert pipeline for upstream on-call.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Harness can run a standardized 30-minute sweep for three model families and produce stable TPS metrics (median, p50, p95, p99, sd).
2) Cold-start variance probe produces repeatable deltas within ±7% after tuning.
3) Bisector can identify a single changed commit or config that explains >60% of observed p95 regression in a run with at least 3x signal-to-noise.
4) Generated reports posted to Confluence and an S3 artifact; CI job exits non-zero on large regressions and opens an ENG ticket with diagnostic bundle.
approach_notes:
- Replace current synthetic driver with a multi-phase load generator: seed (small), warm (steady), spike (microburst), decay (KV-warmdown).
- Implement fixed-random-seed tokenizers so input tokenization variance is minimized.
- Collect per-request traces: model variant, GPU placement, batch size, effective KV cache hit/miss.
- Use bootstrap sampling on windowed p95 to estimate confidence intervals and suppress false positives.
- Bisector will run binary search across candidate commits/infra configs; where multiple suspects exist, it will perform targeted replay tests against each candidate in parallel.
- Provide CLI and library bindings so QA and SRE can run ad-hoc probes locally and in CI.
runtime_infra_implications: Requires short-lived dedicated GPU workers for isolated runs (prefer T4/RTX6000 for cost parity), an S3 bucket for artifacts, and a small DynamoDB table to store run metadata. Estimated incremental cost: ~$400/week during active tuning. Add temporary IAM role for CI runner to upload artifacts.
runbook_snippet:
Command: ./bin/tps-prober --model redwood-gpt-13b --scenario cold-start-sweep --duration 1800 --out artifacts/run-<ts>.tar.gz
Post-run: ./bin/tps-analyze artifacts/run-<ts>.tar.gz --report html --upload s3://redwood-benchmarks/tps/
If p95 delta > configured threshold, the CI wrapper will call the bisector: ./bin/tps-bisect --run artifacts/run-<ts>.tar.gz --candidates git-range.txt
notes: This ticket intentionally targets variance and bisecting rather than raw max throughput; separate follow-ups will optimize kernel selection and batching heuristics. Keep webrtc/streaming tests out of scope for now.
